exposure: Intrauterine administration of everolimus to the pregnant mother
cohort: A single patient diagnosed with Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC)-associated rhabdomyoma detected in utero due to a de novo variant in the TSC2 gene.
finding: Early detection of a pathogenic TSC2 variant, followed by in utero everolimus administration and early vigabatrin therapy, was associated with fetal tumor regression, unchanged SEGA, and a milder developmental delay, despite the development of West-syndrome and therapy-resistant focal seizures.
